guard: a durable join queued on the delivery daemon's ctl.delivery rail behind a running one waits its turn, so a lifecycle's inventory sent before it runs does not list it; only the anycast request ops are answered in their own time
why: The daemon serves ctl.delivery with a concurrent predicate so an anycast request's status, cancel
and takes do not wait behind a channel join. Every other op stays on the in-order chain. If a join
ran in its own time too, a join sent behind a held one would be authorized and written before the
lifecycle's inventory, and the inventory would list a row the deprovisioner then leaves behind.
The suite imports core through its package export, so the command builds core before each run
and the mutation rebuilds it after restore. Without that, the run would grade a stale dist and

mutations.name: every ctl.delivery request is answered in its own time
mutations.expectRed: with a join queued behind a running one, the inventory of the queued join's lifecycle answers an empty list
mutations.cell: with a join queued behind a running one, the inventory of the queued join's lifecycle answers an empty list
mutations.note: The queued join no longer waits for the held one. It runs and writes its row before the inventory, which then lists it.
